lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: Is, as a fiend, confin'd to tyrannize

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: On unreprievable condemned blood.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: O, I am scalded with my violent motion

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And spleen of speed to see your majesty!

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: O cousin, thou art come to set mine eye:

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: The tackle of my heart is crack'd and burn'd;

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: And all the shrouds, wherewith my life should sail,

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: Are turned to one thread, one little hair:

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: My heart hath one poor string to stay it by,

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: Which holds but till thy news be uttered;

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: And then all this thou seest is but a clod,

lines.speaker: King John
lines.text: And module of confounded royalty.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: The Dauphin is preparing hitherward,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Where heaven he knows how we shall answer him;

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: For in a night the best part of my power,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: As I upon advantage did remove,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Were in the washes all unwarily

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Devoured by the unexpected flood.

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: You breathe these dead news in as dead an ear.

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: My liege! my lord!--But now a king,--now thus.

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: Even so must I run on, and even so stop.

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: What surety of the world, what hope, what stay,

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: When this was now a king, and now is clay?

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Art thou gone so? I do but stay behind

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: To do the office for thee of revenge,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And then my soul shall wait on thee to heaven,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: As it on earth hath been thy servant still.--

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Now, now, you stars that move in your right spheres,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Where be your powers? Show now your mended faiths;

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And instantly return with me again,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: To push destruction and perpetual shame

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Out of the weak door of our fainting land.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Straight let us seek, or straight we shall be sought;

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: The Dauphin rages at our very heels.

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: It seems you know not, then, so much as we:

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: The Cardinal Pandulph is within at rest,

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: Who half an hour since came from the Dauphin,

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: And brings from him such offers of our peace

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: As we with honour and respect may take,

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: With purpose presently to leave this war.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: He will the rather do it when he sees

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Ourselves well sinewed to our defence.

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: Nay, 'tis in a manner done already;

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: For many carriages he hath despatch'd

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: To the sea-side, and put his cause and quarrel

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: To the disposing of the cardinal:

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: With whom yourself, myself, and other lords,

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: If you think meet, this afternoon will post

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: To consummate this business happily.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Let it be so:--And you, my noble prince,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: With other princes that may best be spar'd,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Shall wait upon your father's funeral.

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: At Worcester must his body be interr'd;

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: For so he will'd it.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Thither shall it, then:

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And happily may your sweet self put on

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: The lineal state and glory of the land!

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: To whom, with all submission, on my knee,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: I do bequeath my faithful services

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And true subjection everlastingly.

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: And the like tender of our love we make,

lines.speaker: Earl of Salisbury
lines.text: To rest without a spot for evermore.

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: I have a kind soul that would give you thanks,

lines.speaker: Prince Henry
lines.text: And knows not how to do it but with tears.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: O, let us pay the time but needful woe,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Since it hath been beforehand with our griefs.--

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: This England never did, nor never shall,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Lie at the proud foot of a conqueror,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: But when it first did help to wound itself.

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Now these her princes are come home again,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: Come the three corners of the world in arms,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: And we shall shock them: nought shall make us rue,

lines.speaker: Philip the Bastard (Faulconbridge)
lines.text: If England to itself do rest but true.
